html:
The Pyongyang Great Revival was a wave of Protestant fervour that began at a church meeting in Pyongyang, now in North Korea, in January 1907, with mass public confession and prayer.

American Presbyterian and Methodist missionaries had worked in the north since the 1880s. Korea was falling under Japanese control, and many Koreans found hope and organisation in the churches. The revival spread across the country, and Pyongyang became known as the Jerusalem of the East. Kim Il Sung grew up among Christians; his mother was a church member.

Christians led much of the March 1st Movement of 1919. After 1945 the communist government closed the churches, and many northern Christians fled south, where they helped build the large Protestant churches of South Korea, such as the Yoido Full Gospel Church. Religion in the North is now tightly controlled.
